ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human safety review; place both accounts' statements side by side, do not record either as established fact, and keep the trip fare unchanged pending the review.
ruling.reasoning:
This case is filed as a safety dispute. The rider's complaint alleges that during the trip the driver repeatedly commented on her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe [F3][F4]. That is an allegation of unwanted personal advances / harassment made inside the vehicle [SAFE-1]. Under SAFE-1, where such an allegation appears in the complaint, no automatic adjudication is made and the case goes to a human with a factual summary; the policy execution trace records this element as settled (✓ SAFE-1, allowed outcome escalate only) [SAFE-1].

Reading every message and statement in the record: there are no in-app chat messages at all [F3], and the only text from the driver is his post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]. I find no threat, intimidation, sexual remark, hostile or abusive language in any recorded text [F4]. The safety concern in this case therefore does not arise from the recorded words; it arises from the rider's first-person complaint of body comments and a request for her number, of which nothing in the record is a contemporaneous or verbatim account [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Because the clause is engaged by the nature of the allegation and asks a person, not the system, to read what was said, I do not decide the allegation at all [SAFE-1].

The cabin conduct is not recorded anywhere: the chat slice is empty [F3] and no system record (gps [F1][F2], fare, traffic) can speak to what was said inside the car [F1][F2][F3]. The rider's account and the driver's denial [F4] stand opposed and neither is corroborated; a statement cannot be weighed against the other statement by any record rule, since there is no system record of the cabin to prefer to either [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The record therefore cannot settle the central element the clause needs read, which is exactly the situation SAFE-1 assigns to a human reviewer [SAFE-1].

No route issue arises: actual distance 17.1 km against an optimal route of 17.2 km (−0.1 km) [F1], so no off-route segment exists and no RD-2 computation is available or sought [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. No cancellation or waiting fee is in issue, so NS-0/NS-1/NS-6 never enter [F1][F2][NS-1][NS-6]. The fare of $35.70 is the RydeX fixed quote and no fare fact exists to show any unpublished addition, so no monetary relief is computable [F1][FARE-1]. Accordingly the amount is null and the outcome is escalate [SAFE-1].

Profile facts are not used to decide the case: the driver's 327 days, 999 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes [F6] and the rider's clean record [F5] cannot alone determine the safety allegation, and there is no finding against the driver that would engage RD-6 or an account flag [RD-6].

Summary for the human reviewer: (1) what happened — a RydeX night trip, Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point, pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54, 17.1 km driven against a 17.2 km optimal route [F1][F2]; (2) the dispute — the rider alleges the driver commented on her body and asked for her number and that she felt harassed and unsafe, while the driver's only record account is "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]; (3) what to check — there are no chat messages [F3], so the reviewer should obtain the rider's full written account (timing, wording, whether she used any reporting channel) and the driver's account, note that no system record covers the cabin [F1][F2][F3], and confirm neither account is to be recorded as established fact. If the reviewer finds the alleged words amount to unwanted advances, the SAFE-1 conduct standard applies [SAFE-1]. No route, fare or no-show adjustment is proposed [F1][FARE-1][NS-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute type (rider alleges body comments and a request for her number, feeling harassed and unsafe) engaged by SAFE-1, and the record contains no contemporaneous or verbatim account of the words used — empty chat [F3], no cabin system record [F1][F2], and only the driver's post-trip denial [F4]; the case is routed to a human reviewer with the factual summary in the reasoning.

rejected_claims.reason: There is no recorded message from which the judge can read body comments or a request for a number: the chat slice is empty [F3] and the only driver text is a bare denial [F4]; SAFE-1 engages on the allegation in the complaint but does not convert an unrecorded account into a finding, so the harassment is screened, not established, and escalation (not a finding) follows [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The driver does not dispute escalation, but his request that the case be escalated cannot be read as clearing him: SAFE-1 routes the allegation to a person without resolving it, and no record supports a finding that the conduct was appropriate [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The claim that the record 'contains nothing verifiable either way' [F3][F4] is correct only as to the cabin; it does not entitle the driver to any determination in his favour, and the emptiness of the chat cannot be read as his denial being established [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The clean gps figures — 17.1 km against 17.2 km optimal [F1] and a 2.2-minute duration variance [F2] — say only that the car stayed on route; they are not evidence about what was said in the cabin, and do not rebut the rider's safety account [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The absence of traffic or incident facts is neutral; no RD-4 justification is at issue because F1 shows no off-route segment, and the lack of a traffic record cannot be used to discount a verbal-conduct complaint [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-1].
No refund is sought, so the point is moot: the fare is the RydeX fixed quote and F1 shows no excess distance, and no fare fact exists to support or defeat any adjustment [F1][FARE-1].

Conceded as to scope: no RD-2 refund and no NS-1/NS-6 fee finding is available, because there is no off-route segment [F1] and no cancellation or waiting-fee fact in the record [F1][F2][RD-2][NS-1][NS-6].

Agreed on the absence of route or fare issues [F1][F2], but the rider's requested relief is human review of the safety complaint, which is granted through SAFE-1 escalation rather than by any monetary award [FARE-1][SAFE-1].

ruling.evidence_gap: No record of the in-cabin conduct: the chat slice is empty [F3] and no gps, fare or traffic fact covers what was said [F1][F2]; the only driver account is a post-trip statement [F4] and the rider's account is user-submitted, so the SAFE-1 allegation cannot be read or resolved from the record.
